accepted.title: Conformal removability throughout the non-space-filling SLE range
accepted.text: For every κ∈[4,8), is the range of chordal SLE_κ almost surely conformally removable? In the standard upper-half-plane realization from0 to∞, this means that every homeomorphism of the Riemann sphere that is conformal off the trace (including its endpoints) is a Möbius transformation.
accepted.subject: Probability & Random Geometry

accepted.scope_review: Keeps the full parameter range, with provedκ=4 and known nonempty subinterval disclosed. Conformal removability is different from recovering an LQG metric by geodesic gluing. No conclusion aboutκ≥8.
accepted.literature_finding: Kavvadias–Miller–Schoug provesκ=4. accepted.title: Graph-distance scaling limits of mated-CRT maps
accepted.text: For γ∈(0,2), let (L,R) be a two-sided Brownian motion with unit coordinate variances and correlation−cos(πγ²/4). For ε>0 define G^ε on εℤ: for x<y add an edge if max(inf_{[x−ε,x]}L,inf_{[y−ε,y]}L)≤inf_{[x,y−ε]}L, or if the same inequality holds for R. Do there exist deterministic normalizing constants a_ε>0 such that the rooted graph metric spaces (G^ε,a_ε d_graph,0), in the peanosphere coupling, converge in probability in the local pointed Gromov–Hausdorff topology to the γ-LQG quantum-cone metric space rooted at its marked point as ε→0?
accepted.subject: Probability & Random Geometry

accepted.title: Internal mated-CRT diameter exponent agrees with reciprocal LQG dimension
accepted.text: For γ∈(0,2), let (L,R) be a two-sided Brownian motion with unit coordinate variances and correlation−cos(πγ²/4). For ε>0 define G^ε on εℤ: for x<y add an edge if max(inf_{[x−ε,x]}L,inf_{[y−ε,y]}L)≤inf_{[x,y−ε]}L, or if the same inequality holds for R. Let χ(γ)=lim_{ε↓0}log E[diam(G^ε|(0,1])]/log ε⁻¹, where the diameter uses distances in the induced subgraph onεℤ∩(0,1]; this limit is known to exist. Let d_γ be the almost-sure Hausdorff dimension of theγ-LQG metric. Is there some γ_*∈(√2,√(8/3)] such that χ(γ)=1/d_γ for every0<γ≤γ_*?
accepted.subject: Probability & Random Geometry
